events.title: ‘All I want to do is cry’: trauma of 7 October survivors three years after the attacks
events.summary:
Israeli communities shattered by Hamas massacres are torn between rebuilding their lives and remembering lost friends and relatives

Keith Siegel spent many of his long hours in Hamas captivity in Gaza etching everything that happened after 7 October 2023 into his memory. For 484 days, he recited to himself every place he was held, the dates he was moved and every attack or humiliation he endured or witnessed.

He aimed to store intelligence that could help Israeli forces free other hostages if he was released, to keep track of time as the days slid by and be able to tell his family what happened to him. Now his body is free, but he cannot loosen those memories.

events.title: Former UN food agency official claims he was fired for highlighting hunger in Gaza
events.summary:
Benjamin Davis appealing against dismissal from FAO, after being accused by director general of playing ‘political games’

A former senior UN food agency official has alleged he was fired last week for his work highlighting hunger in Gaza, and has launched an appeal against his dismissal.

Benjamin Davis said the leadership of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) had refused to renew his contract as director of its rural transformation and gender equality division because his team had published a brief on hunger in Gaza and held a seminar on the subject last year, and because he had taken part in weekly “moment of silence” vigils on FAO grounds for those killed.

events.summary:
Pakistani authorities insist marchers calling for former PM to be released from jail will not reach the capital

Imran Khan’s supporters have begun a march to Islamabad to demand his release from jail after efforts by the government to halt the protest failed.

The march began in the former prime minister’s stronghold province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in north-west Pakistan on Sunday, according to leaders of his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party.

events.title: India’s Cockroach movement launches new protests over changes to voter roll
events.summary:
Thousands gather in Mumbai with heavy police presence as concerns mount that millions will be denied voting rights

India’s youth-led Cockroach movement kicked off more nationwide protests on Friday as thousands of people gathered in Mumbai, amid mounting concerns that millions of citizens are being unfairly stripped of their vote.

The movement, which calls itself the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) and has massive support among the country’s gen Zs, returned to the streets to demand the resignation of the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar.

events.summary:
Up to 300mm of rain could fall in places, while extreme downpours bring landslides and deaths in Nepal

Torrential rain and potentially damaging flooding are forecast in eastern Spain over the coming days, as cold upper air moves over the warm, humid surface air of the Mediterranean Sea, fuelling violent, slow-moving thunderstorms near Spain’s east coast. The weather pattern, known as a Dana, occurs most often in autumn.

Models show more than 100mm of rain could fall across the region on Friday, with 200-300mm possible in some areas. Cities including Valencia and Castelló de la Plana, are most at risk. Valencia has experienced several damaging floods in recent years. Catalonia has now put three towns under lockdown and Valencia has shut schools for nearly half a million children.

Smit Machchhar says in video call with Indian PM that he realised if he did not get up ‘passengers would lose their lives’

The Indian pilot who helped thwart an apparent attempt to crash a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv said his faith and his desire to save his passengers allowed him to make a “last push” to open the cockpit door as he fought for his life.

Capt Smit Machchhar, who was recovering in an Abu Dhabi hospital, described to India’s prime minister, Narendra Modi, how he helped save the plane and its more than 170 passengers.

events.title: British Sikh activist released from Delhi jail after nine-year detention
events.summary:
Indian government issued with warning it would be in contempt of court if it failed to release Jagtar Singh Johal

The British Sikh activist Jagtar Singh Johal has been released from a Delhi prison after the Indian high court warned the government it would be found in contempt of court if it continued to attempt to keep him in jail despite an 18 September court order releasing him on bail. Johal has been incarcerated for nine years without any full trial.

The court order was issued after Johal’s lawyers issued a writ of habeas corpus alleging he was being detained against the express direction of the court.

Five more former traders who were jailed for rigging interest rates have had their convictions quashed by the court of appeal in London, after a long battle to clear their names.

The court overturned the convictions of Jay Vijay Merchant, Jonathan Mathew, Philippe Moryoussef, Alex Pabon and Colin Bermingham – all of whom worked at Barclays.

events.title: All hail the Kult of Kemi – captain, coach and owner of the Conservatives | John Crace
events.summary:
The Tory leader is now too big for the party to allow her to fail, so everything she does is acclaimed a work of genius

Where’s AI slop when you need it? It could all have been so much simpler. Just ask ChatGPT to write me a leader’s speech in the style of Kemi Badenoch. Make it an hour and 10 minutes long, so plenty of room for padding. Go heavy on the slogans, cliches and the obligatory crap politician jokes. Ones we’ve all heard many times before. Not least at this conference.

Make the usual digs at Labour and put the boot in to Reform. The main aim of the speech is to try to reposition a party that is tanking in third place on 20% in the polls as the main opposition to the government. And just to give everyone a reason to go home with a feeling of mild optimism, chuck in a retail offer at the end. An uncosted tax cut for people who are rich but don’t feel quite rich enough. The new multimillionaire common-or-garden lower middle classes.

Wittington Investments, the holding company of the Weston family that controls the Loblaws grocery chain and Drugmart pharmacy chain in Canada, will own Boots’ UK and Irish retail operations and opticians chain, the No7 beauty brand and a franchise arm in Thailand.

Eleven bail hostels that were supposed to have housed dangerous prisoners during the early release of stalkers and domestic abusers in England and Wales have been closed, the Guardian can disclose.

Seven of the halfway house facilities, known as approved premises, were shut because of a lack of qualified staff, and the other four because of problems such as infestations or lack of running water, Whitehall sources said.

events.title: Tropical Storm Isaias near Mexico is forecast to become a hurricane
events.summary:
Isaias, which succeeded Tropical Depression Nine, would be the first hurricane of the belated Atlantic season

Tropical Storm Isaias formed early on Wednesday in the warm waters off eastern Mexico and forecasters said it was expected to strengthen into the first hurricane of the belated Atlantic season before hitting the US Gulf coast later in the week.

Isaias succeeded Tropical Depression Nine as it strengthened overnight. It was located about 285 miles (460km) west of Progreso, Mexico, and about 580 miles south-west of where the Mississippi River spills into the Gulf of Mexico in Louisiana, according to the National Hurricane Center (NHC). The storm on Wednesday morning had maximum sustained winds of 40mph (65km/h) and was moving east to north-east at 8mph.

events.title: Ireland will boycott Eurovision again because of Israel's participation, but the song contest is still expanding
events.summary: The 2026 Eurovision Song Contest was marred by boycotts in protest against Israel's participation in the midst of its war on Gaza. It still aims to keep growing.

events.title: Germany news: Volkswagen ends collective wage agreements
events.summary: In an effort to cut costs, automaker Volkswagen terminated most of its collective wage agreements in Germany. This could reignite disputes with employee representatives.

events.title: El Nino is a 'postcard from the future' — and could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths
events.summary: The current El Nino could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths. Researchers warn it offers a glimpse of temperatures that may become normal within 20 years.

events.title: Hungary's reckoning with Orban's corrupt system picks up speed
events.summary: Hungary's Prime Minister Peter Magyar vowed to dismantle Orban's corrupt networks. High-profile figures are being arrested and many Hungarians are pushing for swift accountability, but the rule of law takes time.

events.title: South Park satirist pushes for accountability in Cornell gang-rape lawsuit
events.summary: Writer Toby Morton is using a new website to amplify allegations in a high-profile sexual assault lawsuit involving seven Cornell students. The reopening of the case is causing an outcry on social media.

events.title: UK PM Burnham seeks 'hope again' at Labour Party conference
events.summary: Andy Burnham is seeking a delicate balance between optimism and realism at Labour's annual party conference. He promised hope and an end to "politics as usual" but also an "honest conversation" about difficult dilemmas.

events.title: Global trade weathers Iran, Ukraine and Trump's tariffs
events.summary: Over the past six years, COVID, two wars and Donald Trump's tariffs have shaken world trade. With globalization already stalling, is this a temporary shock or the start of a great reversal?

events.title: AI: Concern as Germany plans to double data center capacity
events.summary: Germany is rewriting the rules to attract data center investment from AI companies. But local communities are becoming increasingly skeptical.

events.title: Spain grows fruit and vegetables for Europe, but it's running out of water
events.summary: Spain's southern coast produces up to 25% of Europe's fruit and vegetables. But amid intensive farming, climate change and illegal wells, the water it takes to grow them is drying up.

events.title: What do Manchester City's charges mean for German football?
events.summary: Manchester City have reportedly been found guilty of major financial rule breaches. What does this mean for German football?

events.title: Germany news: COVID vaccine maker BioNTech to close 3 sites
events.summary: COVID-19 vaccine maker BioNTech is to close three sites in Germany after efforts to find buyers failed. Meanwhile, Rhine water levels have fallen to record lows after an unusually dry September. DW has more.

events.title: Diesel prices are surging putting further pressure on Europe
events.summary: Trucks, farms and industry are powered with diesel. Now prices are soaring due to refinery disruptions, supply shortages and geopolitical tensions. A potential US export ban could make Europe's diesel crunch even worse.

events.title: Will Jürgen Klopp's charisma be enough for Germany?
events.summary: After defeat to Greece, Jürgen Klopp faces the first real test of his tenure as coach of Germany's national men's football team. Can his charisma alone push this group forward?

events.title: Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in Nations League match overshadowed by political controversy
events.summary: Ireland easily beat Israel in a Nations League fixture that 24 hours earlier appeared in doubt. One Irish player pulled out of the match to express his opposition to Israel's actions in the Gaza Strip.

events.title: What would Francis of Assisi make of his fame today?
events.summary: The Catholic saint renounced wealth and fame to become a mendicant friar. Yet throughout history, his teachings and life have inspired popes, Dante and even Mussolini.

events.title: Germany news: Are Germans giving up their beloved meat and sausages?
events.summary: Germans used to be all about sausages and meat. While those do remain popular, things seem to be slowly changing. There also are new insights into the economic side of East Germany's espionage DW has more.

events.title: Backlash over data centers tests Europe's AI ambitions
events.summary: Massive data centers needed to run AI are triggering protests across Europe. Their operators counter that they boost digital sovereignty and energy independence.

events.title: DW shows solidarity with Georgians' commitment to democracy
events.summary: Cultural and media professionals in Georgia remain under threat. A DW panel brings together insiders who share their hopes and fears.

events.title: Bundesliga, other top European leagues call for major FIFA reforms
events.summary: The Bundesliga and three other leading European football leagues have said major reforms to world-governing body FIFA are "essential." However, they stopped short of calling for the resignation of boss Gianni Infantino.

events.title: Jürgen Klopp starts Germany job with shaky Netherlands draw
events.summary: A late Netherlands goal denied Jürgen Klopp a win in his first match as Germany coach. The former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund boss has big ambitions, but the game showed he's going to need more time to achieve them.

events.title: Three-way battle for power in world chess: Who will be elected FIDE president in Samarkand?
events.summary: The era of Russian presidents is coming to an end at the World Chess Federation (FIDE). Two Germans and one Kazakh are up for election. Among the issues at play are money, Kremlin influence, and unanswered questions.

events.title: After several difficult years, economists now expect German economy to grow
events.summary: Germany's economy is growing again, but recovery remains on shaky ground. High government spending is keeping the economy afloat, while energy prices, a shortage of skilled workers and debt continue to weigh on it.

events.title: Political psychology: Why extremist parties are thriving and what democratic politicians can do against it
events.summary: Far-right and far-left parties are celebrating success after success, leaving moderate politicians in the dust and worrying many Germans. Political psychology helps us understand what's behind growing polarization.

events.title: Could flattering AI make humanity turn on itself?
events.summary: A study shows chatbots mirror users' politics, part of a broader tendency known as AI sycophancy. Researchers fear this could deepen polarization.

events.title: Germany news: Berlin officially withdraws Olympics bid
events.summary: Berlin's decision to withdraw its Olympic bid means that only Munich and the western Rhine/Ruhr region are left in the running as potential Olympic hosts. DW has more.

events.title: Could a Left Party government in Berlin expropriate large real estate companies?
events.summary: The socialist Left Party won the Berlin election partly on the promise to implement the city's 2021 expropriation referendum as a way to solve the city's rent crisis. But can it really happen?

events.title: China's 13-year-old swimming star raises questions on child athletes
events.summary: Three gold medals and three Asian Games records have catapulted China's Yu Zidi, 13, into the sporting spotlight. She is far from the first teen prodigy, but should teens be competing at elite level?

events.title: Germany's oldest party, the center-left SPD, is in a difficult position following its success in the Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania state election
events.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) has vowed to press ahead with controversial reforms, but resistance is mounting within his coalition partner, the SPD. How much dissent can a governing coalition tolerate?

events.title: Munich and Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr – Germany's two remaining Olympic candidates
events.summary: Munich or the Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr region? Germany aims to host the Olympic Games again. Just two candidates are left after Berlin pulled out at the last minute.

events.title: El Nino explained: How the weather pattern affects hurricanes and tropical storms
events.summary: From drought to major floods and extreme heat, El Nino will have a huge impact on the world's weather. In the Atlantic, it could mean a season without hurricanes.

events.title: China's new travel rules unsettle tech giants and talent
events.summary: Beijing is locking the gates to stop expertise and capital in strategic industries from fleeing. The country accused of industrial-scale intellectual property theft now fears the West will take its own.

events.title: Living in the shadow of LA's hidden oil wells
events.summary: Many lifelong residents of Los Angeles have health impacts from growing up close to oil extraction. Now, the city is trying to close down the worst offenders, but it's an enormous task.

events.title: Could we see MMA at the Olympics?
events.summary: Mixed martial arts has made its debut at the Asian Games this week. It takes the sport closer to the Olympics, but there are doubts about the next step — and the influence of the popular and lucrative UFC.

events.title: Male infertility is 'grossly underreported'
events.summary: It's not all on women anymore — doctors do test men for sperm count and motility. But still too few men get checked, possibly due to a misconception that a healthy sex life means healthy sperm. Spoiler: It doesn't.

events.title: Will Germany have enough gas this winter amid energy supply crunch?
events.summary: Germany's gas storage sites are far less full than in recent years. Officials say supplies are secure, but analysts warn that a cold winter or import disruptions could push prices higher. So how secure is the supply?

events.title: Princess Diana's brother makes explosive claims about royals in new memoir
events.summary: Here are some of the key revelations from Charles Earl Spencer's highly anticipated memoir "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister." It has already provoked Buckingham Palace to react.

events.title: Germany's car crisis: Can the 35-hour workweek survive?
events.summary: German carmakers want employees to work 40 hours instead of the current 35 without extra pay, arguing it would improve competitiveness. Unions strongly oppose the proposal and view it as an attack on workers' rights.

events.title: Germany faces energy tax losses as EV sales rise
events.summary: The rapid shift to electric vehicles in Germany is cutting fuel tax revenue for the government. As EV sales surge, policymakers face growing pressure to find new ways to fund roads and transportation infrastructure.

events.title: Summer of 2026 broke records in Europe, and caused deaths
events.summary: The summer of 2026 was not only the hottest on record in Europe, it also saw a record number of people die. More than 16,000 are thought to have died because of the heat in Germany alone.

events.title: Oktoberfest 2026: Everything you need to know
events.summary: This year, AI will be used to manage overcrowded situations. Find all the numbers surrounding the fest — including the price of water!

events.title: Rebels, workers, radicals: The making of 'Red Berlin'
events.summary: Bloody May, student sit-ins and the squatter movement: Berlin has long been a hotbed for working-class organizing and radical left-wing politics.

events.title: Women's football in Germany booming, but still much to do
events.summary: Women's football is growing rapidly, particularly in Germany. Nevertheless, equal pay and investment remain major talking points.

events.title: Strait of Hormuz attacks spill oil into Persian Gulf
events.summary: As war disrupts one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, satellite images reveal that oil is spreading toward protected coral reefs and mangrove forests.

events.title: Dual citizenship means Germany now in competition for talent
events.summary: Coach Jürgen Klopp has named several players to his first Germany squad who are eligible to play for other countries. Some still aren't committed to playing for thje national team long-term.

events.title: Beethoven and Andy Warhol: Rebel icons on show in Bonn
events.summary: The new exhibition "Beethoven by Warhol" at the Beethoven House in Bonn presents the pop artist's late masterpiece: a picture of Ludwig van Beethoven. The exhibition shares the story of the work with the public.

events.title: VAR's mission creep a problem for football
events.summary: After a decade of use, questions around VAR in football are louder than ever. Has the technology strayed too far from its remit?

events.title: Alexander Ovechkin backs Putin party in campaign video
events.summary: Ice hockey legend Alexander Ovechkin has lent Vladimir Putin's party a helping hand in its parliamentary election campaign. That's in keeping with a pattern of support by an athlete who claims not to be political.

events.title: Klopp wants Germany's football team to 'reclaim the flag'
events.summary: Jürgen Klopp, Germany's new head coach, says he wants his team to reclaim pride in being German after recent political developments.

events.title: Jews once lived lived here: When houses tell stories
events.summary: Time and again, residents tracing the history of their homes discover the lives of Jewish predecessors who fled or were deported amid stories of suffering and loss.

events.title: Jürgen Klopp's first Germany squad includes 44 players
events.summary: Germany's new head coach Jürgen Klopp has named a huge squad for his first four games, splitting them into two groups. A host of new faces is included.

events.title: Saint, sinner or feminist icon: How Mary Magdalene's image evolved through time
events.summary: From "Apostle of the Apostles" to prostitute, Mary Magdalene has been assigned a wide variety of roles, as a new exhibition shows.

events.title: How climate change worsened Nepal's deadly mountain collapse
events.summary: A glacier and rock collapse in Nepal killed nearly 1,400 people and left thousands missing. Scientists say decades of warming helped set the disaster in motion.

events.title: Global Gender Gap Report: Women's hard-won gains 'fragile'
events.summary: Two decades of progress toward gender parity is at risk as women's political representation declines, according to a new World Economic Forum report. At the current pace, the remaining gap could take 120 years to close.

events.title: German drama 'Blindspot Berlin' revisits 2016 Christmas market attack
events.summary: A decade after the terrorist attack on a Berlin Christmas market, a new German miniseries looks into the institutional failures that allowed the deadly truck rampage to happen.

events.title: How extreme heat is hitting wallets
events.summary: Heat waves, wildfires and floods have cascading economic impacts, causing incomes to decline and the price of basic goods to rise. The trend will escalate as temperatures continue to increase.

events.title: Spanish scientists find first evidence of Diplodocus dinosaur in Europe
events.summary: Paleontologists in Spain say they have found the first evidence of the long-necked Diplodocus genus of dinosaur outside of North America. They found bones at the rich La Tejeria fossil site in Teruel in eastern Spain.

events.title: Why the era of cheap government debt is over
events.summary: US debt has topped $40 trillion. How risky is the country's growing debt burden. And will investors keep funding Washington's deficits?

events.title: Why AI researchers warn humanity could face extinction
events.summary: Could artificial intelligence pose an existential threat to humanity? Some leading researchers are warning against an unregulated race toward AI superintelligence.

events.title: Iran and US: Two countries and the pistachio between them
events.summary: The pistachios sold across the United States have a surprising history: California's trees trace their roots to Iran. Now, both regions face the same threat — their farmland is sinking as groundwater disappears.

events.title: Africa's richest man Dangote's IPO out of reach in Nigeria
events.summary: Dangote seeks $1.6 billion from investors to finance a $14.3 billion expansion and thus double the oil refinery's capacity. The offer could give millions of Nigerians a stake in the company. But who can truly afford it?

events.title: The Crusades: How a medieval holy war still shapes politics
events.summary: In 1095, the Catholic Church launched the Crusades: wars that left millions dead and whose legacy still shapes political and ideological conflicts.

events.title: Can Iran replace sea trade with land routes?
events.summary: Iran is shifting trade toward northern ports and land routes as its southern shipping faces a US blockade. Analysts say the corridors can keep essential goods moving, but cannot replace maritime trade.

events.title: Why are European banks moving gold out of United States?
events.summary: The Netherlands and France have moved their gold out of US vaults. Part of the reason is fears about the reliability of the US, but equally important is the need to keep gold closer to home in the event of a crisis.

events.title: Corals as climate archive: Are El Nino events intensifying?
events.summary: Records show that El Nino events have been frequent and often extreme over the past few decades. Is this normal? Or is it the result of climate change? Corals can give us a clear indication.

events.title: India looks to steer BRICS away from anti-Western turn
events.summary: The BRICS summit 2026 takes place in Delhi this weekend. Unlike last year, Putin and Xi are expected to attend. Can India keep the expanded bloc united?

events.title: The 'end of an era' as Goethe-Institut in Russia closes
events.summary: The Goethe-Institut was one of the last German institutions still operating in Russia. However, following Moscow's decision to close its offices, all employees will have to stop working by September 13.

events.title: How Celine Dion became a pop culture icon across generations
events.summary: As the global star kicks off her anticipated Paris residency, here's how Celine Dion managed to gain younger followers while keeping her loyal older fans.

events.title: How Belarusians still find hope in a silenced country
events.summary: The documentary "Letters from the Silenced Country" depicts the ongoing repression under the authoritarian regime. Director Andrei Kutsila talked to DW ahead of the film's Venice premiere.

events.title: Why we're still looking for dark matter
events.summary: When physicists said they may have spotted evidence of dark matter almost 100 years after it was proposed as a theory, the internet lit up. Here's why we're searching for the thing that holds everything else together.

events.title: Conspiracy theories can provide answers but not peace
events.summary: Twenty-five years after 9/11, conspiracy theories about the terrorist attacks persist. But even as an attempt to make sense of a tragedy, psychologists say the benefit in conspiracy ideation or belief is short-lived.

events.title: The billion-euro trade driving Europe's eels to extinction
events.summary: Traffickers are making big bucks smuggling millions of critically endangered eels across continents, using suitcases on planes and legal loopholes to deliver them to dinnerplates. Where are the smuggling hotspots?

events.title: The Bayeux Tapestry in London: What's behind the hype?
events.summary: The exhibition of the Bayeux Tapestry at the British Museum is eagerly anticipated across the UK, as the medieval masterpiece is considered by many to be a symbol of the country's identity.

events.title: US woman who survived botched execution is conscious, speaking
events.summary: The woman who survived a failed execution in a US prison last week is now conscious and speaking, but her prognosis remains unclear, her lawyers said on Tuesday. Christa Pike, 50, who was sentenced to death for a murder she committed when she was a teenager, received two supposedly lethal doses of the drug pentobarbital at a Tennessee prison a week ago.

events.title: Scars from Oct. 7 fuel deep divisions over Netanyahu ahead of Israeli election
events.summary: As Israel gears up for its first elections since Hamas' Oct. 7, 2023, attack, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his opponents are putting it at the heart of their campaigns. Three years on, the worst security failure in Israel’s history now threatens to end the career of its longest-serving prime minister. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.

events.title: African tourists cancelling trip as xenophobia shadows South Africa's appeal
events.summary: South Africa has recorded record tourist arrivals over the past two months, with more than one million visitors arriving by air each month. But behind these encouraging figures, a concern is emerging: African tourists may gradually turn away from South Africa, even as tourism accounts for more than 8% of the country’s GDP. The country’s xenophobic image has left its mark, as FRANCE 24’s team on the ground reports.

events.title: Brit adventurer back on UK soil after 28-year round-the-world walk
events.summary: British adventurer on a 50,000-kilometre, 28-year trek home from South America without using any transport has set foot on UK soil after swimming the Channel, his publicists said Tuesday. Karl Bushby, a 57-year-old former paratrooper, set off from Punta Arenas, Chile, in November 1998, vowing to reach his mother's home near Hull in northern England without travelling on planes, trains, boats, vehicles or other transport modes.

events.title: New Comoros law bans foreign nationals from certain jobs
events.summary: A new law in the Comoros bans foreign nationals from running certain small-scale businesses, threatening the livelihoods of thousands of people, most of them Malagasy. A measure that mirrors a growing wave of economic protectionism targeting migrant workers across the continent.

events.title: A new 'Les Mis': This week in French film
events.summary: This week on arts24, film critic Manon Kerjean takes us through some of the latest French cinema releases, starting with a new adaptation of Victor Hugo's "Les Misérables". Vincent Lindon plays Jean Valjean, opposite Tahar Rahim as Inspector Javert in a three-hour epic that brings a thriller-like tension to the classic story.

events.title: What we know about espionage, treason allegations against Germany's ex-spy chief
events.summary: A court on Wednesday ordered the former head of Germany's foreign intelligence service August Hanning to remain in pretrial detention after his arrest on suspicion of espionage and treason, along with a former deputy who allegedly supplied him with secret files. Here's what we know about one of the biggest security breaches in German history.

events.title: From Mai 68 to 2026: France’s long student protests tradition
events.summary: Students, parents and trade unions were demonstrating across France Tuesday, protesting what they say is under-investment in high schools. From Mai 68 to the CPE crisis in 2006, major French student and youth protests have pressured leaders and transformed national politics.

events.title: The secrets behind Mali junta’s takeover of Kidal without a fight
events.summary: The Malian army says it has entered the strategic northern city of Kidal, which was captured around five months ago by Tuareg separatists who announced their withdrawal earlier Tuesday as the military advanced – a symbolic boost to Mali's junta and its Russian backers. In late April, jihadists from Al-Qaeda-linked JNIM and its Tuareg separatist allies kicked off a series of attacks aimed at weakening Mali's junta rulers, including taking control of Kidal and killing the defence minister. FRANCE 24’s Senior journalist Wassim Nasr explains.

events.title: Why American artist Mary Cassatt's legacy still resonates in France today
events.summary: In this edition we're pleased to welcome back Lauren Jimerson to discuss the Mary Cassatt exhibit entitled "The Choice of Independence" that's currently showing at the Musee d'Orsay in Paris. Lauren is an art historian and author, specialising in modern art and women artists. She tells us why Cassatt was a key figure in the Impressionist movement and why this exhibition is so important.

events.title: Russia warns against spreading 'false information' as reports emerge of second plague case
events.summary: The World Health Organization joined Western leaders on Wednesday in urging Russia to share more information about what killed a plague institute worker in Siberia as reports emerged of a second suspected case. The Kremlin said Moscow had shared what it knew and accused the media ​of spreading "false information".

events.title: China's evolving funeral practices: From traditional burials to cremation
events.summary: This year, China released new rules for funeral practices. The government is putting an emphasis on affordable and environmentally friendly funeral services. It's part of a decades-long reform to promote cremation. But in a country where burials are deeply rooted in local traditions, how are these attempts to modernise funerals being perceived? FRANCE 24's Yena Lee reports.

events.title: 'Great moral courage: The French thought they knew de Gaulle and suddenly realized they didn't'
events.summary: François Picard is pleased to welcome Julian Jackson, the British historian, author and Emeritus Professor of Modern French History at Queen Mary University of London. His biography of General de Gaulle laid the foundation for France’s two-part biopic, "De Gaulle: Résistance". And on the heels of this surprise box-office hit, Jackson’s book is now available in French: La Chute : France 1940. He takes us back to the occupation of Paris and the extraordinary collapse of France in the summer of 1940.

events.title: October 7: Former Israeli hostage speaks to France 24
events.summary:
“The terrorists pulled us out through the window. They handcuffed me and pushed us into a car that they had brought from Gaza.”
 
Former Israeli hostage Shoshan Haran speaks to France 24.

events.title: French parents join school protests to support and protect their children
events.summary: Widespread protests swept across France on Tuesday over anger at the state of the country's school system. The police responded with tear gas and water canons when some on the fringes of the marches turned violent. Among the demonstrators were parents who came to march alongside their children to support their cause – and, for some, to ensure their children could protest safely. After several teenagers were injured, they feared further clashes.

events.title: Three years on, October 7 massacre sites in Israel draw visitors seeking to remember
events.summary: Three years after the October 7 attack, when Hamas militants killed at least 1,195 people in Israel – mostly civilians – the sites of the massacre near the Gaza border have become heavily visited memorials. They offer Israelis and Jews in the diaspora a place to honour those who were killed, as FRANCE 24’s Stéphane Amar reports.

events.title: Three years on, questions remain over what Netanyahu knew before October 7
events.summary: As Israelis mark the third anniversary of the October 7 Hamas attack, and with elections due later this month, one question keeps resurfacing: What did Benjamin Netanyahu know in the run-up to the attack? The Israeli prime minister has been accused of ignoring repeated warnings – an allegation he denies.

events.title: Devastation in Gaza: Three years of war reshape the enclave beyond recognition
events.summary: Three years ago, the war between Israel and Hamas began. In Gaza, it has meant three years of bombardment that have dramatically transformed the Palestinian territory. Residents of the enclave try to survive the best they can, caught between hope for a better future and resignation.

events.title: October 7, hour by hour: How the Hamas attack on Israel unfolded
events.summary: On October 7, 2023, Hamas launched a series of deadly attacks on Israeli towns and military sites near the Gaza border in a massive, coordinated assault. We look back, hour by hour, at how the events unfolded that day and how it has become known as the biggest massacre that the Jewish state has ever seen.

events.title: French wine output set to hit historic low after record summer heatwaves
events.summary: The French agriculture ministry on Wednesday forecast a historic low wine output this year after a summer of record high temperatures and a reduction in cultivated areas. The total harvest plunged 14 percent below the 2021–2025 average, with the Champagne region hit hardest due to an early harvest after the heat increased a sugar buildup.

events.title: 'Time doesn't heal': Parents of October 7 attacks victim Aner Shapira
events.summary: The parents of a 22-year-old Israeli man who was killed when Hamas attacked the Nova music festival on October 7, 2023 have told FRANCE 24 how they can still feel him surrounding them even though he's no longer here. Shira and Moshe Shapira say that time doesn't heal, but they are learning how to live with their loss. Their son Aner managed to throw seven grenades back towards Hamas fighters, before an eighth exploded in his hands, killing him. They spoke to us in Perspective.

events.title: Three years after October 7 attacks, Israel's economy shows its strength
events.summary: After shrinking briefly in the aftermath of the October 7, 2023 attacks, Israel's GDP is predicted to grow by 4 percent this year. The country's tech sector – specifically its defence startups – has played a big part in this performance but challenges, notably demographic ones, are on the horizon. Meanwhile, the destruction caused by Israel's war in Gaza has reduced GDP per capita in the Palestinian enclave by 83 percent and reconstruction plans there have yet to begin.

events.title: October 7: Israelis mark three years since Hamas attacks
events.summary:
Israel is marking the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023, Hamas terrorist attack on Wednesday with memorials across the country.
 
At the site of the Nova music festival, where more than 300 people were killed, families gathered at dawn for a moment of silence and paid tribute in front of portraits both of festival-goers and security forces who died on October 7.

events.title: France suspends stun grenade use at student protests ahead of PM speech
events.summary: France has suspended the use of stun grenades by police at student-led demonstrations, the interior minister said Wednesday, as allegations of police brutality mounted after days of sometimes violent demonstrations across the country. Tens of thousands of people took to the streets across France on Tuesday demanding better conditions in high schools. That same evening, President Emmanuel Macron held an emergency meeting with Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu and other key ministers to find a way out of the crisis. FRANCE 24's Antonia Kerrigan reports from a high school in Aubervilliers, France.

events.title: Russia claims there is no epidemic risk after death of plague institute worker
events.summary: Russia's health watchdog has claimed there is no risk of an epidemic following the death of a plague institute worker in Siberia - as the Kremlin accuses the media of providing false information about the case.

events.summary: A man has been arrested after seven people were injured in an attack at a school in Poland.

events.summary: Lionel Messi was on the scoresheet as he played his final game for Argentina on an emotional evening in Buenos Aires.

events.title: Plague risk to UK 'very low', officials say after Russian woman's death
events.summary: The risk to the UK from plague is very low, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has said, after the death of a laboratory worker in Russia who may have been exposed to pneumonic plague.

events.title: Paramount completes $81bn takeover of Warner Bros Discovery
events.summary: Skydance-owned Paramount has completed its $81bn (£61bn) takeover of Warner Bros Discovery - bringing together the two media giants under a combined company.

events.title: A British father asks a Cyprus judge to avoid prison after son's fatal hotel fall
events.summary: The lawyer for a British man who pleaded guilty to a charge of negligence in the fatal fall of his 3-year-old son from a hotel window in Cyprus has appealed to a judge to avoid a prison sentence

events.summary: Spain has lifted the arrest warrant for Catalan separatist leader Carles Puigdemont, allowing the politician to return home without fear of detention for the first time in nearly a decade

events.summary: Two commercial vessels have been hit by drones in the Black Sea, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev

events.summary: British police have arrested a 22-year-old man in London on suspicion of a terror offense linked to Iran

events.title: Colombia's president offers support to veterans extradited to US over Haitian leader's killing
events.summary: Colombian president Abelardo de la Espriella has offered legal assistance to a group of Colombian military veterans who were arrested over the 2021 killing of Haitian president Jovenel Moïse

events.title: Heavy rains pummel St. Vincent and the Grenadines, forcing school closures
events.summary: The government of St. Vincent and the Grenadines has shuttered all schools after heavy rains unleashed flooding and landslides across the eastern Caribbean island

events.summary: Zambia plans to sign a revised health agreement with the United States that excludes controversial clauses about sharing patient data and specimens

events.summary: A stronghold of Turkey’s opposition has fallen to President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s ruling party for the first time

events.summary: The Ebola outbreak in Congo is spreading rapidly to new hot spots where patients have little or no support

events.title: Serbia ties overseas voting to local time, a move likely to spark backlash ahead of a key election
events.summary: Serbia's election commission has tied overseas voting hours to local time, affecting the Serbian diaspora's ability to vote in the upcoming election later this month

events.title: Nepal ends search for flood victims as family reactions range from anger to relief
events.summary: The families of thousands missing after Nepal's catastrophic floods have mixed feelings about the government's decision to stop search efforts
